articles.title: In 2017, Sweden replaced a motorway’s top-layer stone with steel slag; 7 years later, the 200-metre test road had comparable overall performance, but deeper rutting
articles.summary: Discover how Sweden is paving the way for sustainable road construction using steel slag, a byproduct of the steel industry, as an alternative to traditional asphalt. Learn about the benefits and long-term performance of this innovative material after seven years of testing.
articles.body: Steel mills produce massive mounds of waste material each year, and quarries are finite. Because studded winter tyres erode asphalt faster than most other wear factors, road builders in Sweden have to be picky about what goes on a motorway's surface. Engineers on the E4 near Jönköping had to try something a little different because of that tug of war.They chose a material called slag, which is the stony residue left over from melting down scrap steel in an electric arc furnace. Most of it already has a use in Sweden, and the steel industry group Jernkontoret estimates that just over 80 per cent of the slag produced in the country is reused. But the same group admits that this kind of slag remains an untapped resource for creating asphalt.So when they repaved the E4 through Huskvarna in August 2017, a research team recognised an opportunity to test the concept at full scale. In one portion, they replaced the native stone in the top layer with crushed steel slag, a stretch of around 200 metres. Seven years on, the stretch was still in use, and the results make for compelling reading for anyone who cares about greener roads.How the test road was builtThe test was conducted on a busy section of the E4 just north of Jönköping, with Lake Vättern on one side and hillside residences on the other. According to Trafikverket, the motorway has two lanes each way and a speed restriction of 90 km/h. Some 26,000 vehicles use it per day, and one in six are big vehicles. The slag was in the slow lane, where most lorries go, with about 18,000 vehicles a day, a fifth of which are heavy.The surface is double-layer porous asphalt, designed to reduce traffic noise. It has a 30 mm top layer lying on a 50 mm bottom layer, and the slag replaced stone just in the top one. The builders used a slag product called Smedjebacken, supplied by NCC, in diameters between 4 and 11 mm, and contractor Svevia laid it on the same days as the ordinary pavement beside it. The slag mix required less binder by weight, at 4.5 per cent compared with 6 per cent for the stone version. It also retains its dark grey hue for life, so the road appears fresher than it is and the markings are more visible after dark.Findings from seven yearsThe results are from Ulf Sandberg, a researcher at the Swedish National Road and Transport Research Institute, who presented them at a noise engineering conference in 2024. The Swedish Transport Administration, Trafikverket, financed the work. The paper has been published on the research webpage of the agency.In fresh condition the slag surface reduced tyre noise by around 7 dB compared to the conventional Swedish reference surface, which corresponded to the stone version. Its noise reduction was comparable to or slightly better than the standard double-layer pavement after five to seven years. The results had startled Sandberg; the slag surface was clogging up a little faster. After four years, the water drainage test took 86 seconds on the slag surface and 47 seconds on the stone surface. Sandberg thinks tiny pores among the slag particles may help balance things out.Other figures gave a similar tale. For both surfaces the Transport Administration accepts wet friction ratings of between 0.60 and 0.64 for fresh asphalt. Rolling resistance on the slag was roughly 2 per cent lower in 2018, but that differential was too minor to count as a real change. Rutting was the one field where slag lagged behind. By 2022, the wheel tracks in the slag part were 10.8 mm deep compared to 7.8 mm in the stone section, a difference that the report says is negligible and nonetheless acceptable.A notable moment came in May 2023. The road authorities repaved the conventional part of the highway after six years but left the slag section alone, possibly because it appeared to be in better shape. By summer 2024 it had hit the seven-year mark, and no repaving was in the works for that year.What this means for highwaysBecause slag is heavier than natural stone, it takes more to bring it to the asphalt plant and subsequently to the site. The team also had difficulty hitting the air voids target, ending up slightly over 20 per cent instead of the expected 25, which may have contributed to the earlier blockage. Sandberg says the density disparity means slag blends must be constructed differently, but he thinks that improved material selections and proportions could enhance the outcome.The upside is that it is a bigger upside. Steel slag is a waste item that can leak heavy metals in countries with substantial stockpiles, but the report adds that leaching is insignificant when slag is sealed into asphalt. In some situations high-grade natural aggregates are also becoming scarce. Separate research from VTI looked at ten slag products from various Swedish companies and found most met or surpassed the standards for road aggregate.The lesson for now is small yet useful. A test road in Sweden, about 200 metres long, has shown over a seven-year period that steel slag can, in at least this case, replace natural stone in the top layer of a busy roadway and perform roughly the same as a traditional surface, according to the researchers behind the study. One disadvantage is that it causes slightly deeper ruts. Larger tests will show whether the idea can be implemented, but early results suggest that this waste product can perform well on the road.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: US House Speaker Johnson weighs 'next chapter' if Republicans lose majority-Fox News
articles.summary: WASHINGTON, Oct 8 (Reuters) - Republican US House of Representatives Speaker Mike Johnson told Fox News he does not know if he will remain in politics if his...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON, Oct 8 (Reuters) - Republican US House of Representatives Speaker Mike Johnson told Fox News he does not know if he will remain in politics if ‌his party loses control of the chamber in next month's congressional election even ‌as he insisted his focus was on protecting the party's majority.

"Heaven forbid, if we lose this majority or whatever, ​I don't know what my next chapter of life is," the Louisiana lawmaker told Fox News.

Johnson has repeatedly predicted that Republicans would defy history and grow their House majority in the upcoming election. But he has on occasion held out the possibility of a Republican loss in ‌efforts to raise money and ⁠turnout, predicting that a Democratic majority would mean another Trump impeachment.

The latest comments appeared to be his public acknowledgment that his caucus could face defeat ⁠in November.

"If God moves on our hearts and says we should, you know, go back to my hometown of Shreveport and start a lawn business, I'll do that with equal fervor. I mean, ​I ​just want to be of my highest and ​best use ... to God and to ‌my country," Johnson said, Fox News reporter Aishah Hasnie said on X.

His comments come as US voters are already heading to the polls in a number of states to vote early ahead of the November 3 election day, with rising prices and the Iran war looming large as Americans weigh Republicans' grip on Congress and fellow Republican Donald Trump in the ‌White House.

Reuters/Ipsos polling shows 44% of registered voters saying ​they would vote for Democrats while 37% say they ​would vote for Republicans and 13% ​undecided. Nearly two-thirds of US adults nationwide, or 65%, said they disapprove ‌of Trump's term since taking office for ​a second time in ​January 2025, compared to 32% who said they approve.

Johnson said he was not to blame if Republicans lose their legislative majority, telling Fox: "If we lose the House, it ​will be because the ‌people were misled."

"I'm traveling nonstop," added Johnson, who scheduled the House to be in ​recess until after the election. Trump has also begun campaign-trail rallies.

(Reporting by Susan ​Heavey; editing by Scott Malone and Deepa Babington)

articles.title: Donald Trump honours CEO Satya Nadella as JD Vance goes hard at Microsoft
articles.summary: TOI correspondent from Washington: On the same day US vice president JD Vance put Microsoft in the crosshairs over its use of foreign workers, his boss
articles.body: TOI correspondent from Washington: On the same day US vice president JD Vance put Microsoft in the crosshairs over its use of foreign workers, his boss Donald Trump was preparing to honour the company’s CEO, Satya Nadella, with America's highest technology awards at a White House ceremony.Asked about the award for Nadella as he announced the strike against Microsoft, Vance said that the administration didn’t want to harm the company but send them a message that they ought to hire Americans over foreign workers.“So we’re going to continue to support Microsoft and have a great relationship with Microsoft, but we’re also going to deny them the ability to apply for these permanent residencies until they show that they are going to get serious about putting American workers first,” he said.Nadella, who has headed Microsoft since 2014, was born in Hyderabad, India, and moved to the United States for graduate studies before rising through Microsoft’s ranks to become its chief executive.There is another distinctly Indian dimension for Vance himself. His wife, Usha Vance, is the daughter of Indian immigrants whose family roots are in Andhra Pradesh.Her parents, Krish and Lakshmi Chilukuri, moved to the US around 1980 and built academic careers in San Diego, California. The Chilukuri family has deep roots in the Visakhapatnam region of Andhra Pradesh.And the connection comes full circle in Hyderabad, the city where Nadella was born and where Microsoft established its India Development Centre in 1998, making it the largest research and development centre outside its Redmond headquarters, employing some 20,000 professionals.“Our message to Microsoft is: You’re a great American company, but you’ve got to hire great American workers,” Vance said.You use AI every day. articles.title: Fire alarm disrupts Northwestern 'October 7' play based on massacre survivor testimony
articles.summary: A fire alarm forced evacuation during Northwestern University's "October 7" play featuring Hamas attack survivor testimony at Cahn Auditorium.
articles.body: A fire alarm at Northwestern University in Evanston, Illinois interrupted a play recounting firsthand testimony from survivors of the Oct. 7 Hamas terrorist attacks on Tuesday night, forcing an evacuation of the auditorium during a performance intended to commemorate the victims ahead of the massacre's third anniversary. The performance, titled "October 7," was hosted by Northwestern Hillel and featured verbatim testimony from survivors and eyewitnesses of the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas-led terrorist attacks, which killed approximately 1,200 people in Israel and resulted in 251 hostages being taken into Gaza. Northwestern Media Relations told Fox News Digital that the fire alarm was activated during the performance at Cahn Auditorium, prompting an evacuation and a police investigation. "At approximately 8:12 p.m., a fire alarm at Cahn Auditorium was activated, which caused the evacuation of the building," a Northwestern Media Relations spokesperson said. "Upon a fire and police investigation, the building was determined safe, and guests invited back in. The event continued as planned and concluded at 9:45 p.m. The Northwestern University Police Department will continue their investigation." FORMER HAMAS HOSTAGE COUNTERS HASAN PIKER’S UT AUSTIN EVENT WITH HER STORY OF SURVIVAL A spokesperson for Campaign Against Antisemitism condemned the broader climate facing Jewish students on college campuses in a statement provided to Fox News Digital. "Campuses have become radicalized, resulting in the ostracization of Jewish students on campus," the spokesperson said. "Universities in the U.S. and throughout the West have to take a stand against antisemitism on campus. Administrative leave is a start, but if the allegations are borne out, the consequences need to be severe. That’s what zero tolerance means." The earliest widely circulated version of the video, which shows attendees evacuating the auditorium as a fire alarm sounded, was posted by Ann McElhinney, co-writer of the play "October 7," who said in her post that the alarm hit "even stronger because it’s already October 7 in Israel." ANTI-ISRAEL GROUPS RALLY ACROSS US ON OCTOBER 7 ANNIVERSARY, CHANTING 'LONG LIVE THE INTIFADA' McElhinney's co-author and husband, Phelim McAleer, called for those responsible to face consequences in an interview with the Jewish News Syndicate on Wednesday. "The people responsible must be found and prosecuted," McAleer said. "These people are demonic. Disrupting the truth, disrupting stories of tragedy and heroism. They should be ashamed of themselves. This just makes us all the more determined to take this play to every campus across America." The Coalition Against Antisemitism at Northwestern (CAAN) shared a statement on its website, saying that the timing of the alarm was particularly troubling because the 2023 massacre began amid rocket attacks and air raid sirens warning Israeli civilians to seek shelter. CAMPUS ANTISEMITISM EXTENDS BEYOND STUDENT PROTESTS AND INTO CLASSROOMS, ADL WARNS However, the group emphasized that investigators had not established whether the alarm was deliberately activated. It said the Cook County State's Attorney's Office Hate Crimes Unit was aware of the incident and called for authorities to examine whether antisemitic bias played a role. The incident came less than a year after Northwestern reached a $75 million agreement with the Trump administration to resolve federal civil rights investigations involving allegations of antisemitism and discrimination on campus. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Under the November 2025 agreement, Northwestern committed to strengthening protections for Jewish students, implementing mandatory antisemitism training and maintaining policies governing demonstrations and disruptions of university activities. The production, created by McAleer and McElhinney and directed by Jeff Gurner, previously ran off-Broadway and was performed at several universities, including Princeton, UCLA and Bowdoin College.

articles.title: Indian-origin doctor mom arrested and charged in Florida as she watched 7-year-old drown. She said she froze, she was not strong enough to pull him from water
articles.summary: A Louisiana doctor, Sukanthini Subbiah, has been arrested by the Orlando Police Department in Florida and charged with first-degree aggravated
articles.body: A Louisiana doctor, Sukanthini Subbiah, has been arrested by the Orlando Police Department in Florida and charged with first-degree aggravated manslaughter as she was present when seven-year-old Khushil Bandi drowned. The incident took place on April 10 but the arrest was made on Wednesday. The 48-year-old Indian-origin doctor is being held without bond in the Orange County Jail and she faces up to 30 years in prison if convicted.Subbiah was visiting her mother in Orlando with her own seven-year-old son identified as DJ by the police. DJ became friends with Khushil and his twin sister who lived in the neighborhood. Khushil and his twin sister were supposed to be under Subbaiah and her mother's watch one evening and they went to a pool. Immediately, the three children jumped into the pool. Subbaiah told the police that she noticed that Khushil had been underwater for 45 seconds or so. She asked the other two to look for him but they said the water was too deep. Subbaiah sought help from another man who jumped into the water and pulled out Khushil, who was unconscious at the time.Subbiah said she did not waste any time but surveillance footage revealed that she did not do anything for a long time.Seven minutes and two secondsSurveillance footage revealed that they arrived at the pool at 6.19 pm. At 6.20 pm, Khushil could be seen playing in the pool and Subbiah was not seen in the footage. Seven seconds later, Subbiah was seen in the footage. About a minute later, Khushil sank to the bottom of the pool. After another minute and half, Subbiah went to the edge of the water and was seen "standing and staring at the center of the pool". For another minute, she did not do anything and then asked his son what happened to Khushil.Three minutes later, Subbiah got into the water but stopped at knee height.Then she approached another man for help. The man jumped and brought Khushil in 50 seconds. The total time between the boy being completely submerged and being removed from the water was seven minutes and two seconds, police said.7 days later, Khushil was deadKhushil was rushed to a hospital in a critical condition. After three days, he had no brain activity and he had swelling in his brain and was suffering from seizures. He was taken off life support on April 17 and pronounced dead. An autopsy report concluded that his cause of death was ruled as complications of drowning.When police interviewed Subbiah, she allegedly said that she 'froze' and thought she was 'going to pass out' after noticing Khushil had been submerged for an extended period. She also allegedly said she believed she was not strong enough to pull the seven-year-old from the water, which is why she asked for help.Investigators concluded that Subbiah had the opportunity to alter the outcome.You use AI every day. articles.title: A $132,000 GoFundMe was raised for radio host Ronn Owens; federal review found thousands spent on mortgages, businesses and family transfers
articles.summary: A $132,000 GoFundMe campaign created amid radio host Ronn Owens’ health problems became the focus of a federal review after he and his wife sought
articles.body: A $132,000 GoFundMe campaign created amid radio host Ronn Owens’ health problems became the focus of a federal review after he and his wife sought bankruptcy protection. Court records examined by the US Trustee showed that only about $17,000 of the money was used for medical and pharmacy expenses, while much larger amounts went towards mortgage payments, contributions to businesses and other spending. The review did not result in criminal charges against Owens or his wife, but it raised concerns about whether donors received what they expected from the campaign.What happened to the $132,000 Ronn Owens GoFundMe donationsThe GoFundMe campaign was launched in January 2025 as Owens faced serious health problems. The longtime KGO radio host had described living with Parkinson’s disease for 23 years, along with four bouts of cancer, including colon cancer, and serious heart issues. The campaign appealed to people familiar with his long broadcasting career and said donations would help Owens and his family through difficult circumstances.According to TheDesk, GoFundMe ultimately paid Owens and his wife, Elizabeth Naylor, $132,480 from the campaign. The US Trustee Program in Phoenix later reviewed more than 18 months of financial records, including the bank account into which the donations were deposited. The examination found that the money was largely spent on expenses unrelated to medical care.The federal review found most spending went elsewhereThe figures examined by the trustee provide the clearest picture of how the money was used. TheDesk reported that around $17,000 went towards medical-related bills, although it was not clear whether all of those expenses were connected specifically to Owens’ cancer treatment. By contrast, $118,898 was identified as spending unrelated to medical needs.More than $61,600 went towards mortgage payments, while nearly $44,400 was recorded as capital contributions to companies owned by Owens. The remaining spending included travel, subscriptions and cash given to a child. SFist also reported that other money went towards credit card bills and transfers to family members.The amounts were significant because the campaign had been presented against the backdrop of Owens’ worsening health and financial difficulties. The trustee’s review looked beyond the original fundraising appeal and followed the money through the couple’s accounts.Why did the bankruptcy case become part of the disputeThe GoFundMe spending came under scrutiny during Owens and Naylor’s bankruptcy proceedings. The couple first sought Chapter 13 bankruptcy protection, but later filed under Chapter 11 after the earlier case did not provide the protection they sought. Their bankruptcy proceedings eventually brought their financial records under closer examination.SFist reported that during the period covered by the review, the family had more than $20,000 in monthly income and spent more than $520,000 from its bank accounts. The trustee found that only a relatively small portion of the couple’s financial burden was connected to medical expenses.The US Trustee then argued that the bankruptcy case should be dismissed. TheDesk reported that the trustee’s attorney pointed to the bank and GoFundMe records when assessing the couple’s ability to meet Chapter 11 requirements. The court ultimately agreed that there was no reasonable likelihood of a successful reorganisation.The court also examined family transfers and other expensesAnother part of the financial review concerned money transferred to Owens’ daughter, Laura Owens. RadarOnline reported that financial records showed $19,608 in gifts to her, despite the couple having stated under oath that they had not made gifts worth more than $600 per person during the relevant period.The records also showed spending on consumer credit cards, retail and online purchases and other non-medical expenses. RadarOnline noted that the government did not bring criminal or civil fraud charges against Owens or Naylor, and they were not formally accused of fraud in court.The family transfers received additional attention because Laura Owens had her own legal and financial troubles. RadarOnline reported that she had filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy, which was later dismissed, while SFist described her as financially dependent on her parents. Those circumstances formed part of the wider financial background examined during the bankruptcy proceedings.What did the judge decide about the bankruptcyThe federal bankruptcy court ultimately dismissed Owens and Naylor’s case and prevented them from filing another bankruptcy action for at least two years. TheDesk reported that Chief US Bankruptcy Judge Madeleine Wanslee cited significant failures to meet Chapter 11 requirements, along with multiple errors and misstatements in the record.The judge also pointed to changes in sworn statements concerning ownership of the home where the couple lived. Naylor agreed to the two-year restriction but disputed the suggestion that the documents and testimony demonstrated wrongdoing. According to TheDesk, she said she was grateful for the donations and had worked with the court in the interest of transparency.The ruling did not determine that the GoFundMe spending itself amounted to criminal wrongdoing. Instead, the judge allowed donors to pursue possible claims against Owens and Naylor in state court. Creditors were also allowed to resume collection efforts.The fundraising questions remain separate from criminal chargesThe federal trustee said the financial records raised a serious question about whether GoFundMe donors received what they believed they were supporting. SFist reported that the trustee did not conclude that a law had been broken. The issue of whether the fundraising appeal and subsequent spending created legal claims was left for donors and GoFundMe to pursue outside the bankruptcy case.The campaign itself remained online at the time of SFist’s August 3 report and had raised about $137,000 against a $140,000 goal.You use AI every day. articles.title: Nashik mourns the loss of a beloved son-in-law
articles.summary: Nashik mourns veteran actor Nana Patekar’s demise, remembered as its beloved “son-in-law” for family ties, visits, theatre support, and farmer advocacy.
articles.body: Nashik: Veteran actor Nana Patekar’s sudden demise has plunged fans and admirers in India and abroad into mourning, but in Nashik, the loss is deeply personal. To many in the district, he was more than a celebrated performer — he was Nashik’s beloved son-in-law.In 1978, he married Neelakanti, whose family lived in the Mumbai Naka area. Her brother, writer Shrikant Haldule, was one of Patekar’s close friends. Over the years, his frequent visits earned him the affectionate reputation of Nashik’s beloved son-in-law, residents recalled.One of his last memorable visits to Nashik came at All India Farmers’ Literary Meet in Mohadi on March 4, 2024. Standing before a gathering of farmers, Patekar delivered the kind of blunt, unsparing speech that had become his trademark. Questioning the indifference towards agriculture, he asked why the prices of wheat and rice remained stagnant while gold continued to soar.“Farmers feed the nation, yet are forced to fight for their own survival,” he said, urging cultivators to rise above caste and religious divisions and build the political strength needed to shape governments, not merely vote for them.A local BJP office bearer who attended the event recalled another candid remark from Patekar. “Politics is not my cup of tea,” the actor had said, joking that political parties would throw him out the very next day because he could never stop speaking his mind.The residents also remembered his contribution to Marathi theatre. As president of 80th All India Marathi Natya Sammelan held in Nashik in 1997, Patekar used his position not to celebrate stars but to spotlight backstage technicians and theatre workers, the often-forgotten backbone of every cinematic production.His generosity resurfaced in Sept 2000, when organisers Prashant Junnare and Kailas Patil brought the play ‘Purush’ to Nashik. Starring Patekar and Ayesha Jhulka, the production was a major event, with tickets priced at Rs 1,000, an unusually high sum at the time. But before the curtain rose, Patekar announced that the entire surplus after expenses and artists’ fees would be donated to Baba Amte’s Anandwan, then facing financial challenges.Even after becoming a national icon, Patekar’s relationship with Nashik never faded. articles.body: A U.S. Marine Corps aircraft carrying four service members burst into flames Thursday following a hard landing during a training mission in North Carolina. articles.title: America has enjoyed the greatest free lunch in history: Vivek Wadhwa reacts to Green Card crackdown on 8 IT companies, says they aren't the visa abusers
articles.summary: Indian-American entrepreneur Vivek Wadhwa strongly reacted to the Donald Trump administration's suspension PERM program for eight IT giants, including
articles.body: Indian-American entrepreneur Vivek Wadhwa strongly reacted to the Donald Trump administration's suspension PERM program for eight IT giants, including Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, TCS, Wipro, HCL Technologies, and Capegemini and said that these companies are not the visa abusers. The visa abusers are those who recruit for these companies or the IT bodyshops and they need to be shut down, Wadhwa said."America has enjoyed the greatest free lunch in history: highly educated, highly skilled immigrants bringing their talent to its shores. Now it’s snatching defeat from the jaws of victory by turning away the truly best and brightest. These companies aren’t the visa abusers. The body shops exploiting the system are the ones that need to be shut down," Wadhwa said, defending Silicon Valley.Suspending PERM process means the H-1B visa holders working in these companies can't take the Green Card route. However, it is not known whether the suspension will eventually be lifted.Nasscom, the apex body of Indian IT companies, called it a temporary suspension and said that it believes that immigration and skilled talent mobility are two separate issues and should not be viewed through the same lens."The H-1B visa program has historically played an important role in addressing short-term skill gaps in the US, and it will continue to be used to address short-term talent gap. However, over a number of years, Indian technology companies have significantly reduced their dependence on H-1B visas, while steadily expanding local hiring and building a strong domestic workforce in the US. They work with majority of the US Fortune 500 companies..."Microsoft only files H-1B petitions for those...Microsoft also issued a statement against the damaging allegation of visa fraud and said Microsoft only files H-1B petitions for those who meet the rigorous standards of this visa category. "We pay our employees some of the highest compensation in the tech sector, and our wages are among the highest of all H-1B filings. We pay our H-1B employees the same as any other employees doing comparable work," it said.Microsoft said it is ready to provide additional information to the administration. "For example, of the approximately 6,000 H-1B visa applications we submitted in the last fiscal year, 80% percent were to extend or change the status of existing Microsoft employees. These were not to hire new people. The remaining filings for new employees were for individuals already legally in the United States who decided to come work for us, and they equal only 1% of our U.S. workforce. They are not new arrivals to our country," it said.JD Vance on IT bodyshopsJD Vance, in his statement, mentioned the IT bodyshops that recruit the H-1Bs on behalf of these IT giants but the administration decided to shake the big players to make an impact, instead of chasing the thousands of small staffing companies."If you are working as an H-1B visa in the United States of America, you’re earning $20,000 less than an American citizen hired in the same position. If you were brought in by one of these foreign outsourcing firms, you’re making $48,000 less than an American citizen in a similar position. So I’m sure that everybody here understands the game that is being played. You bring in indentured servants from outside the country, you lay off American workers and, if you’re a corporation, you make a ton of money by undercutting the wages of American workers, replacing them with people who frankly shouldn’t be in the United States of America to begin with," Vance said.You use AI every day.
